claims.text: Attachment 32 of the 1995 report is Lt. McAndrew's synopsis describing Project Mogul, the top-priority classified balloon-borne experiment programme advanced as the explanation for the Roswell Incident.

claims.text: Marcel was the 509th Bomb Group intelligence officer who collected debris at the Foster ranch with CIC Capt. Sheridan Cavitt, and was photographed with debris at Fort Worth on 8 July 1947.

claims.sourceText: USAF, 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1995)
claims.text: MOGUL was a then-classified top-priority programme of balloon-borne experiments, described at length in the Air Force's 881-page 1995 report by Col. Richard Weaver and 1st Lt. James McAndrew.

claims.sourceText: USAF, 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1995)
claims.text: Ramey, with Col. Thomas DuBose and weather officer Irving Newton, publicly identified the Roswell material as a weather balloon with a radar reflector on 8 July 1947, retracting the RAAF announcement the same day.

claims.sourceText: USAF, 'The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1994)
claims.text: The 1994 USAF report attributed the debris to Project Mogul Flight No. 4, launched 4 June 1947 from Alamogordo, and acknowledged that the weather balloon explanation was a cover story.

claims.sourceText: USAF, 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction' (1995)
claims.text: The announcement was retracted the same day at Fort Worth by Brig. Gen. Roger Ramey, with Col. Thomas DuBose and weather officer Irving Newton identifying the material as a weather balloon with a radar reflector.
